policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'were sons born' is passive; the qere niphal and the ketiv consonants (read as a passive 'were born') both yield that English, and the verse carries no textual note. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
ASV transliterates the name as 'Abigail', with the -ai- that reflects the yod of the qere אביגיל; the ketiv consonants אביגל would give 'Abigal'. The English spelling distinguishes the reading.

Qere תחתיו and ketiv תחתו are the same suffixed preposition spelled plene/defective; ASV 'on his behalf' fits either. The note 'Or, where he was' is alternative_rendering and does not decide a reading. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
ASV transliterates the father's name as 'Laish', which reflects the qere ליש; the ketiv consonants לוש cannot yield that spelling. The 'other' note concerns Palti/Paltiel, not this unit.
Qere מובאך and ketiv מבואך are the same noun 'coming in' with a transposed vowel letter; ASV 'thy coming in' fits either and the verse has no textual note. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
